note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 50; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 7) on data/benches/carbonate.json: a carbonate decomposed. Malachite is weighed by difference into a dish, heated until black, cooled and weighed again: Cu2CO3(OH)2 -> 2 CuO + CO2 + H2O keeps 2 x 79.55 / 221.12 = 72.0 % of its mass.
title: Experiment: what heat takes from a carbonate

steps.title: The empty dish
steps.text: Click the dish to pick it up, then click the balance. Write down what it reads: the empty dish.
steps.why: This balance reads to 0.01 g. Rather than taring it, you weigh the dish empty, then with the sample: the sample is the difference. Every later weighing is taken the same way, so the balance's own small error cancels.

steps.title: About 1.5 g of malachite
steps.text: Pick up the jar, then right-click the dish for the menu. Type 1.5, then click "tip 1.5 g of the solid". Write down the new reading: dish and malachite.
steps.why: Malachite is a basic copper carbonate, Cu2CO3(OH)2: green, and 221.1 g a mole.

steps.title: Off the balance, a burner under it
steps.text: Pick up the dish and click a free square of the bench. Then pick up the burner in Supplies and click the dish.

steps.title: Full flame
steps.text: Right-click the burner, drag its valve fully open, then click 60x on the clock.
steps.why: Above about 300 C malachite comes apart: its carbonate leaves as carbon dioxide and its hydroxide as steam, and black copper oxide stays.

steps.title: Until it is black
steps.text: Watch the green powder darken to black.

steps.title: Flame off, burner away, cold again
steps.text: Right-click the burner, drag its valve shut, and put the burner away: carried back to Supplies, it goes to Storage. Wait until the dish's thermometer reads 20 C.

steps.title: Back on the balance
steps.text: Pick up the dish and click the balance. Write down the reading: dish and oxide.
steps.why: What is left over what you put in: 2 CuO (159.1 g) from one Cu2CO3(OH)2 (221.1 g) is 72.0 %. Your two differences should come within the balance's 0.02 g of that.
